actors.outcome: Agent skill actor responsibilities remain explicit across package changes.
actors.motivation: A skill package needs named authors, executors, reviewers, users, and owners to preserve authority.
actors.proof: Agent skill research and decision records identify each actor and allowed action.

objects.outcome: Every agent skill object has one owner and a proved role in the package result.
objects.motivation: A skill package cannot validate or restore objects whose ownership is implicit.
objects.proof: Agent skill inventories and lifecycle records cover every declared object.

actions.outcome: Agent skill actions advance a declared package state through one task path.
actions.motivation: A skill package needs bounded create, update, validation, recovery, and retirement behavior.
actions.proof: Agent skill task and invocation receipts trace every action to its outcome.

states.outcome: Agent skill states distinguish baselines, candidates, acceptance, rejection, blocks, and restoration.
states.motivation: A skill package cannot make safe transitions when current state is ambiguous.
states.proof: Agent skill records name the prior, candidate, and resulting state.

invariants.outcome: Agent skill purpose, behavior, authority, proof, and portability survive every lifecycle phase.
invariants.motivation: A skill package change is invalid when it trades away a protected property.
invariants.proof: Agent skill baseline and acceptance checks show no invariant regression.

variants.outcome: Agent skill domain variants stay distinct while shared package rules remain stable.
variants.motivation: A skill package must preserve use-case differences instead of flattening them into boilerplate.
variants.proof: Agent skill domain-swap and term-removal attacks fail when specificity is lost.

interfaces.outcome: Agent skill frontmatter, files, tasks, CI, and eval interfaces retain tested contracts.
interfaces.motivation: A skill package can look correct while an executor-facing boundary is broken.
interfaces.proof: Agent skill interface tests exercise real commands, exits, and artifacts.

authorities.outcome: Agent skill mutations and side effects remain within the user's authority.
authorities.motivation: A skill package must not infer permission for purpose changes, deletion, publication, or deployment.
authorities.proof: Agent skill decision records name the authority and block unauthorized branches.

failures.outcome: Agent skill failures are detected at their lowest owning package boundary.
failures.motivation: A skill package needs explicit failure modes to avoid false completion.
failures.proof: Agent skill RED cases reproduce each material failure before repair.

recoveries.outcome: A rejected agent skill candidate can restore the last accepted package state.
recoveries.motivation: A skill package experiment must not leave a slower or less correct state behind.
recoveries.proof: Agent skill rollback receipts match the frozen accepted digest and checks.

evidence.outcome: Every accepted agent skill claim points to current, scope-matched proof.
evidence.motivation: A skill package shape or stale receipt cannot prove domain task success.
evidence.proof: Agent skill evidence records connect sources, commands, results, limits, and freshness.

time.outcome: Agent skill work reaches verified acceptance quickly without stale evidence.
time.motivation: A skill package loses value through avoidable delay or outdated dependencies.
time.proof: Agent skill receipts retain timestamps, wall time, version, and freshness decisions.

resources.outcome: Agent skill resource choices fit measured access and mutation patterns.
resources.motivation: A skill package should reduce CPU, memory, storage, network, cache, context, cost, and attention waste.
resources.proof: Agent skill experiment records measure applicable resources or justify non-use.

quality.outcome: Agent skill quality improves without regressing correctness, speed, simplicity, or judgment.
quality.motivation: A skill package optimization is invalid when another protected dimension worsens.
quality.proof: Agent skill Pareto checks retain only nonregressing candidates.

terminology.outcome: Agent skill terms keep one stable meaning across instructions, files, tasks, and evidence.
terminology.motivation: A skill package becomes hard to execute when one concept has conflicting names.
terminology.proof: Agent skill semantic review and domain contracts reconcile every retained term.

exclusions.outcome: Agent skill exclusions block unsupported facts, side effects, host assumptions, and proxy judgment.
exclusions.motivation: A skill package needs explicit non-goals to avoid authority and scope expansion.
exclusions.proof: Agent skill negative evals and decision records reject excluded behavior.
